visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 current portable/source-terrain frames. Individual Glasgow Cathedral has a long high nave/choir, lower lean-to aisles, crossing transepts, northern ancillary ranges and a square open belfry carrying a tall tiered octagonal stone spire. Pale copper roofs, paired clerestory lancets, larger aisle fields, stepped buttresses/pinnacles, great west pointed glazing with circular tracery, recessed wood portal and small gable oculus establish its exterior. Corrected the west portal/window overlap, lowered lean-to joins so they no longer bury clerestory glazing, moved east lower-church windows onto the exposed chapter face and moved a chapter field away from the attached sacristy. Added the low northern entry and south-range end window. Deep paired belfry cavities, source-terrain thresholds and smaller crypt fields are visible. Temporary restoration scaffolding is excluded.
